newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends near lows after heavy U.S. selling.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends near lows after heavy U.S. selling.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures ended close to session lows on Monday after selling in the U.S. thwarted earlier efforts to push the spot contract above $20.00.

May Brent closed at $19.52 a barrel, just off the intra-day low of $19.48. May became the new front month on Monday and had earlier pushed up to $19.97 a barrel in thin volume in an effort to fill the gap left by the expired April contract.

But a weak opening by NYMEX crude and its failure to breach key technical resistance brought the whole oil complex under pressure, which was reinforced by heavy selling by a single Wall Street trader.

"We began to see some very good Wall Street selling. (One trading house) was selling a lot of paper through different brokers and they looked like they were selling here as well," said one broker in London.
Some dealers said that last week's sporadic gains were overdone.
"I see very little to get excited about on the buy side. I think they saw it as a good selling opportunity," said one.
IPE gas oil earlier closed firmer, but off session highs as forecasts of a late winter cold snap in the North-eastern United States failed to buoy NYMEX heating oil.
April gas oil closed $1.25 a tonne up at $170.75, off a session high of $173.25 a tonne. The gains took the May Brent/gas oil crack spread to $3.40 a barrel.
